# protocol/

Language-neutral protocol files shared by every Syncky component: the relay, the phone app, the agents and the servers. When a vector and prose disagree on byte-level behavior, the vector wins.

**Do not edit generated files by hand.** `types.json`, `units.json`, `messages.json` and every vector file except the RFC 9180 one are generated by the Syncky core and checked against it there; the schemas and the RFC file are hand-written. Table generation derives message types, marker mappings and size limits from protocol definitions and checks canonical field order and both AAD uses against existing vectors.

| [`healthkit-inventory.md`](healthkit-inventory.md) | every HealthKit data kind of the iOS 27 SDK with its read and write model, typical wire size and what Syncky does with it | people |

## Relay queue capacity

`GET /v1/messages` (E11) may include an optional outer `queue` object alongside `messages`, `next_after`, `has_more`, `undelivered` and activity metadata. Updated relays emit it on every successful agent or device page, including empty and paginated pages:

```json
{
  "queue": {
    "hub_bytes": 12000000,
    "sender_rows": 206,
    "max_hub_bytes": 67108864,
    "max_sender_rows": 10000,
    "as_of": "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

| Field | Units and scope |
| --- | --- |
| `hub_bytes` | UTF-8 bytes of general-lane stored bodies across every sender, including unmarked data/control and ordinary system rows; excludes marked traffic, its derived expiry events, delivery-row overhead and the delivered `seq` field |
| `sender_rows` | General-lane stored rows sent by the authenticated caller, counted once regardless of recipient count; excludes marked traffic and its derived expiry events; an agent never sees a phone's row count |
| `max_hub_bytes` | Configured hub byte cap; default 67108864 bytes (64 MiB) |
| `max_sender_rows` | Configured per-sender row cap; default 10000 rows |
| `as_of` | Relay UTC observation timestamp, sampled in the same transaction as the page and usage |

Usage values are nonnegative safe integers; caps are positive safe integers. Stored bodies include expired unswept rows and held rows until deletion. Fetching alone frees no capacity. A transport acknowledgement or committed successful webhook delivery frees a body only when its final delivery is removed; maintenance, purge and revocation can also remove bodies. `undelivered` remains a per-recipient display aggregate and activity's live waiting count excludes expired rows; neither substitutes for capacity accounting. A snapshot describes observed storage, reserves no space and can change before the next upload.

`POST /v1/messages` (E10) adds `details.reason: "queue_full"` only when the caller's stored-row cap or the hub's byte cap refuses a new envelope. Both refusals retain HTTP 429, `Retry-After: 300` and this body:

```json
{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Too many requests","details":{"retry_after_s":300,"reason":"queue_full"}}
```

An identical accepted-body retry still returns `200` with `duplicate: true` before capacity enforcement. Unmarked data/control and ordinary system rows share the general caps. Marked traffic and its unmarked derived expiry events use separate diagnostics accounting; E11 adds no diagnostics queue snapshot. Diagnostics quota/cap refusals use the distinct reasons documented below. Other rate limits retain their existing details without this reason; a 300-second delay alone does not identify a full queue. Fetches and transport acknowledgements remain available subject to their ordinary limits.

Both additions are optional for compatibility: old clients ignore unknown outer fields/details, and new clients accept pages and errors without them. An absent snapshot means unknown usage, not zero; an absent reason retains ordinary rate-limit handling. These fields do not alter envelopes, encrypted inner messages or control reasons. There is no existing outer MessagePage or generic HTTP-error JSON schema/vector to update; `envelope-shape.json` covers submitted envelopes. The minimal server handles direct webhook delivery and has no relay page/error mirror. The generated-file rules and vector precedence above remain unchanged.

## How the agent reads these files

The thin agent loads its bundled or signature-verified message table and inner schemas together with the skill. Optional `send --validate` compiles the available local schema with bundled Ajv 2020; receiving validates transport/authentication and a JSON object with a string `type`, preserving unknown fields without feature-schema parsing. It performs no unit conversion, Health policy checks, series reassembly or summaries. [`agent/src/protocol-files.js`](../agent/src/protocol-files.js) resolves standalone vector files relative to the package; `SYNCKY_PROTOCOL_DIR` selects another copy for selftest.

`syncky-agent selftest` checks crypto, keys, envelope shape/AAD/markers, pairing, App Attest clientData and webhook signatures (exit 4 on failure). Feature normalization, command policy and reassembly belong to phone/schema conformance tests; agent vector tests prove raw preservation. [`agent/AGENTS.md`](../agent/AGENTS.md) describes the transport boundary and [`agent/docs/REFERENCE.md`](../agent/docs/REFERENCE.md) lists limits and errors.

## Vector files and case naming

Pair and webhook link parsers accept exactly `syncky`, `syncky-dev` and `syncky-staging`, case-sensitive. Builders default to `syncky`, preserving production link bytes. Core parsing is independent of the app build: the app refuses pair links for another build before pairing, while webhook paste/scan accepts all three schemes. Tapped webhook links open the build registered for that scheme and require review and explicit confirmation before adding a server. The scheme does not change relay trust policy.

- Generated vector files are `{"format":1,"generated_by":"syncky-core GenerateProtocolArtifacts","cases":[…]}`. `keys.json` is a map `agent`/`dev1`/`dev2`/`mallory` → `{ikm, sk, pk, member_id}`; the RFC file keeps the upstream hex layout.
- Binary values are unpadded base64url; RFC data stays hex. In `app-attest-client-data.json`, `body` encodes the exact request bytes (empty is `""`) and `client_data_sha256` encodes the 32 digest bytes; hashes embedded in `client_data` are lowercase hexadecimal text. On the App Attest wire, Apple's `key_id`, `attestation` and assertion object use standard base64 with padding, while `challenge` and the pairing `public_key` use base64url. This file contains no Apple objects. Compare private keys across libraries through the derived public key: `sk` and `sk_e` are the raw, unclamped RFC 9180 `DeriveKeyPair` output.
- Case `name`s are lowercase snake_case (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$`), unique within a file, and describe the input. Report failures by case name, not by index; regeneration may insert cases.
- `app-attest-client-data.json` uses `attestation_*` and `assertion_*` names with lowercase letters, digits and underscores only. Dispatch by `kind` (`attestation` or `assertion`); every case expects the exact UTF-8 `client_data` bytes and their `client_data_sha256`, without JSON parsing or reserialization of the decoded `body`. All fixtures are public and synthetic; replay checks canonicalization only and adds no agent attestation support.
- Classify cases by their expectation field, never by name. `valid_*` / `valid*` prefixes mark most accepting cases in `envelope-shape.json`, `pair-uris.json` and `webhook-signatures.json`, but some accepting cases are named after the rule they exercise (`created_at_lowercase_t`, `duplicate_key_last_value_wins`, `unicode_body`, `empty_body`). In `pair-uris.json`, `build_*` cases carry `input` and the canonical `uri` instead of `expect`. `series-parts.json` names the kind and the situation (`route_missing_a_part`, `heartbeat_series_in_reverse_order`). `inner-messages.json` uses `sync_*` / `commands_*` for parseable messages (`sync_drop_*` and `commands_drop_rules` exercise element drops), `invalid_*` / `unsupported_*` for message-level failures and `system_*` for system messages; the `system_*` and `diagnostics_*` cases carry `kind` (`data` or `control`, the envelope kind the parser is told; absent means `data`). `fingerprints.json` has the three key-pair cases plus `extra_*` edge cases; `pair-codes.json` has one secret with the three device keys (same code, three proofs) plus `extra_*` cases for a zero-padded group, both orders of the decoy offsets and a decoy that wraps past 999. `envelopes-negative.json` names the mutation (`tag_byte_flipped`, `hub_changed`, `kind_data_relabelled_as_control`, …) and carries a prose `mutation` field. `bridge-json.json` groups cases by `kind`. `command-policy.json` names the type and the rule (`water_millilitres`, `cholesterol_milligrams`, `conversion_overflows_to_infinity`). `webhook-requests.json` names the format first (`native_*`, `hae_*`, `csv_*`, `influx_*`).
- Expectation fields: `envelopes-negative.json` `expect` is the open error code (`aead_failed`, `hpke_open_failed`, `malformed`, `not_a_recipient`, `unknown_sender`); `envelope-shape.json` `expect` is the relay response (`status`, plus `error`/`field` for 400 or `member_ids` for 404); `inner-messages.json` `expect` is `ok`, `invalid` or `unsupported_version`; `series-parts.json` `expect` is `ok`, `incomplete` or `inconsistent`: `series` is the whole boundary sample (no `part`/`parts`), `parts` the wire parts cut at `max_part_bytes`, `reassembled` the whole sample they give back, `conflicts` extra wire parts that differ from a committed one, and `arrival` the order in which `{"part": i}` and `{"conflict": i}` reach one device's reassembler; `webhook-signatures.json` `expect` is `valid`, `bad_signature` or `stale`; `command-policy.json` `expect` is `allow` or `reject` (with `reason`), and an allowed quantity write carries the converted `value` and the catalog `unit`. `webhook-requests.json` has no `expect`: each case carries the destination, its `secrets`, the `collected` changes and `max_request_bytes` in, and the `requests` (with their anchor `groups`) and the `report` counts out; a native body is the canonical sync message of the install `device` plus a `delivery` object; an `hae` case adds the delivery's `session_id` (the `session-id` header of every request) and its bodies are Health Auto Export `{"data":{"metrics":[…],"workouts":[…]}}` with deletions and unmapped types counted in `dropped`; a `csv` body is RFC 4180 rows under the fixed header and an `influx` body is line protocol, both without a `delivery` object, with the object kinds counted in `report.skipped_kinds` (0 for native and HAE). Every `destination` carries `send_deletions`; `accept_writes` and `write_types` are left out because they do not change a request. Every case also carries `link`, the webhook configuration link of its destination and secrets, with the selected scheme (default `syncky://webhook`).
- Optional case-level `resend` in `webhook-requests.json` is a Boolean delivery input, default `false`. When true, every native request adds `delivery.resend: true` before size fitting and signing; false omits the field. HAE, CSV and Influx keep their bodies and headers, Check connection never adds the marker, and export files have no `delivery` block. Delivery indices/counts and `more` cover one delivery call even when a chosen-period operation uses several calls. Resend cases include signed split native requests and unchanged non-native bodies.
- Optional native-only `summaries` in `webhook-requests.json` is a separate direct-history input, alongside unchanged `collected`. Request/report `summaries` counts are independent of raw `samples` and default to zero when absent; summary-only requests may have empty `groups`. The signed summary-only, mixed and split cases retain per-call `more`, index and count semantics. Supporting receivers replace by `(device, type, unit, start, end, stat)`; legacy inner parsers ignore the array. See [server.md](server.md#daily-quantity-summaries-in-native-history) for compatibility.
- `bridge-json.json` adds `core_tools_export_fragment` for encoded native/HAE/CSV streams and recursive envelope descriptors, and `webhook_delivery_report` for the direct-history result. Fragment streams contain already encoded elements/CSV rows. Envelopes provide prefix, suffix, separator, optional stream id, children and whether an empty container is required, so file writers can spool streams and assemble a single document with bounded copy buffers. Native omits an empty summary array; CSV emits one header and escaped/formula-protected CRLF rows in day-stream order. Native/HAE fragments preserve document semantics; CSV preserves parsed row multisets rather than global type order. Raw-object, daily-summary and expected-format-omission counts are separate. Streamed local files publish only when finished and retry the entire original period after error/cancellation; direct-server restart uses the last complete day after cool-down. See [full-depth periods and local files](server.md#full-depth-periods-and-local-files) for foreground and byte/count semantics.
- Optional `url_scheme` is a builder argument: in `pair-uris.json` it belongs only to build `input`; in `webhook-requests.json` it is case-level and selects the scheme of `link`. Its closed enum is `syncky`, `syncky-dev`, `syncky-staging`; absence means `syncky`. Pair parse output never includes it, so exclude it when comparing build input to parsed fields. Both pair versions have parse/build cases for all three schemes; webhook scheme selection leaves request bodies and headers unchanged.
- Compare JSON results structurally (key order free, numbers by value; `command-policy.json` values are doubles that the JVM and JS spell differently), except where a case says byte-exact: pair-URI `build_*` `uri`, the positive envelopes' `enc`/`wrapped_key`/`ciphertext` on re-seal, `webhook-signatures.json` `signature`, and `webhook-requests.json` request `body`, `headers` and `link` (the signature covers the exact body bytes; header order is the order the core sends).

## [KMP-defined] rules other implementations must mirror

The Syncky core defined these details where the wire spec left them open; the vectors pin each relevant implementation's behavior. Transport implementations mirror envelope, authentication and pairing rules. Phone parsers and consumers that normalize Health data or reassemble parts mirror the corresponding feature rules. The thin agent retains raw incoming JSON without applying that normalization, policy or reassembly.

- **App Attest clientData** (`app-attest-client-data.json`): join UTF-8 fields with one LF and no trailing LF. Attestation fields are `syncky-attest-v1`, the unchanged `challenge`, `hub_id`, unchanged `public_key`, and lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 `pairing_token`. Assertion fields are `syncky-assert-v1`, uppercase `method`, the actual URL pathname (including any base prefix, excluding query), lowercase hex SHA-256 of the decoded `body`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bearer `token`, and canonical nonnegative decimal `timestamp_ms` (no sign, leading zeros or exponent). Hash those exact clientData bytes with SHA-256 for Apple. Request-body whitespace and Unicode bytes remain significant; the empty DELETE body hashes zero bytes. The timestamp is part of the hashed input, so changing it changes the digest. The assertion header is `<timestamp_ms>.<standard-base64 assertion object>`; the vector's digest encoding does not change that wire encoding.
- **Envelope shape pointers** (`envelope-shape.json`): the first failure wins, in this order: unparsable or non-object → `field: ""`; first unknown top-level key in document order, then first missing key in the order `v, msg_id, kind, from, created_at, recipients, nonce, ciphertext` → `/<key>`; then `v` (value-based integer 1, so `1.0` and `1e0` pass), `msg_id` (UUIDv7), `kind` (`data` or `control`, case-sensitive), `from` (= caller), `created_at` (RFC 3339 accept form); `recipients` (array of 1..7) and then per index `/recipients/<i>` (not an object), `/recipients/<i>/<key>` (unknown, then missing in the order `member_id, enc, wrapped_key`; bad, duplicate or equal to `from`; `enc` 32 bytes; `wrapped_key` 48 bytes); `/nonce` (12 bytes), `/ciphertext` (≥ 16 bytes). Recipients not in the active member set → `404 unknown_recipient` with all of them in `member_ids`, in recipient order, matched by string only. 413 (including the 4096-byte cap of a `control` envelope, checked after every 400 rule and before 404) and idempotency are relay-only and not in the vectors. A case carries either `envelope` (send its compact serialization) or `raw` (send the exact text).
- **Strict JSON** (`envelope-shape.json` `raw_*` cases): a body outside RFC 8259 is unparseable (`field: ""`), including a leading BOM (Fetch `text()`/`json()` strip it silently, so the relay must check the first bytes itself) and nesting deeper than 128 containers. Duplicate keys keep the last value, as `JSON.parse` does. Unknown-key pointers use RFC 6901 escaping (`a/b` → `/a~1b`, `m~x` → `/m~0x`, the empty key → `/`).
- **Inner parsing, `normalized` and `dropped`** (`inner-messages.json`): message-level `invalid` vs `unsupported_version` (`v` checked before `type`); invalid elements are dropped and listed as JSON pointers (`/samples/3`, `/deleted/0`, `/acks/1`, `/commands/2`) while the message stays `ok`. `normalized` is the canonical re-emission: all four sync arrays and `more` present, unknown fields removed, timestamps in the emit form, integral numbers as integers, ack `version` omitted when absent, command fields kept raw (unknown keys after the known ones) except known-field timestamp normalization and a non-finite number becoming `null`. "Present" means the key exists, so `samples: null` or `more: null` is `invalid`. A `normalized` value parses back to itself (an unknown system type drops `/type` again on re-parse).
- **System messages** (`inner-messages.json` `system_*`): parsed with the envelope kind. In a `control` envelope the eight named types are strict (exact key set, closed `reason` enums, `resync_request.from` emitted in the canonical UTC form, `agent_info.version` matching `^[0-9A-Za-z.+_-]{1,64}$`, `pair_proof.proof` canonical base64url of exactly 32 bytes); any other type matching `^[a-z_]{1,32}$` is `ok`, normalized to `{"v":1,"type":…}` with `/type` in `dropped`; `sync`/`commands` and anything else are `invalid` at `/type`. In a `data` envelope a system type is `invalid`.
- **Control envelope AAD** (`envelopes.json` `control_*`, `envelopes-negative.json` `kind_*_relabelled_as_*`): `syncky-v1|<hub>|<msg_id>|<from>|control`; unmarked data AAD has no suffix, so changing `kind` either way fails with `hpke_open_failed`.
- **Open errors** (`envelopes-negative.json`): checked in the order `not_a_recipient` → `unknown_sender` → `malformed` (only the receiver's own `enc`/`wrapped_key`, then `nonce`, then `ciphertext`) → `hpke_open_failed` → `aead_failed`; a successful open whose plaintext fails the inner parser yields `inner_invalid` or `unsupported_version`.
- **Pair-URI errors** (`pair-uris.json`), first failure wins in the order scheme, host, fragment, duplicate key, encoding, `v`, `unsupported_version`, missing `r h t k n`, missing `c` (v2), value checks `r h t k n`, `c` (v2), `s`, `insecure_relay`: `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_uri","param":<p>}` where `param` is the offending query parameter (`v`, `r`, `h`, `t`, `k`, `n`, `c`, `s`) or `scheme`, `host`, `fragment`, `encoding`; `unsupported_version` for `v` other than `1` and `2`; `c` is a known key in both versions (a duplicate or badly encoded `c` fails like any known key), its value is checked (canonical base64url of exactly 16 bytes) and returned as `pair_secret` only for `v=2`; `insecure_relay` for `s=http` when `allow_insecure` is false. Unknown parameters are ignored, `+` is a literal plus, and `n` is limited to 64 UTF-16 units (JS `.length`). Builders emit `v, r, h, t, k, n[, c][, s]`, `v=2` with `c` exactly when given a secret and `v=1` otherwise, and percent-encode everything outside the RFC 3986 unreserved set with uppercase hex.
- **Pairing code and proof** (`pair-codes.json`): the code hashes the base64url text of `c` (not its bytes) and the proof is keyed by the 16 raw bytes of `c` over the base64url key strings; the choices are the last group and its two decoys as 3-digit strings sorted ascending, so the phone shows the same order everywhere; agents compare a received proof with the expected one in constant time on the decoded 32 bytes.
- **Trusted `ApplyCommand` fields**: `from` and `sync_identifier` come from the envelope sender and the hub, never from the agent. A `from` or `sync_identifier` key inside an agent's command is kept in the stored raw command but never reaches `to_apply`, so an agent cannot address HealthKit objects written for another hub or agent.
- **Command policy** (`command-policy.json`): first failure wins: unknown type, `write: false` or not allowlisted → `type_not_allowed`; a write (never a delete) whose type is outside the case's `scope.write` list, or any write when `scope.write` is `"none"` → `type_not_in_scope`; unknown op; the value not a finite JSON number; `unit` present but not a string or not in the catalog unit's family (an absent `unit` is the catalog unit, `"unit": null` is not); a missing or malformed `start`/`end`, `start > end`, an `end` later than the case's `now` + 1 h or `end − start` longer than the type's `max_span_s` (all `invalid`); then the value is converted with `((value * from.factor + from.offset) - to.offset) / to.factor` in IEEE doubles, in exactly this order (the same unit leaves it unchanged), and checked against `min` and `max` → `value_out_of_range`. A finite value whose conversion overflows to infinity is `value_out_of_range`, not `invalid`. Category writes keep the enum check; deletes skip the value checks. A case's optional `scope` is a full scope object (`read` and `write`, no other keys, each side `"all"`, `"none"` or a list of catalog names, `write` names writable), the grammar `setAgentScope` and `CoreTools.evaluateCommandInScope` accept; a case without it is evaluated with all/all.
- **Canonical `to_apply`**: an allowed write reaches Swift and the ledger with the converted value and the catalog unit (unchanged when the agent already used it), so iOS writes in the catalog unit and the agent's unit is not kept on the phone.
- **Ack statuses** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_ack_deleted_by_user_kept`, `sync_drop_ack_rules`): `applied`, `rejected` and `deleted_by_user`; `reason` (`type_not_allowed`, `type_not_in_scope`, `value_out_of_range`, `healthkit_denied`, `invalid`; `sync_ack_type_not_in_scope`) is required for `rejected` and forbidden for the other two (dropped as an element); any other status drops only that ack. An implementation that does not know `deleted_by_user` must still drop just that element, which is what makes the status backward compatible within v1.
- **Agent scope** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_scope_*`, `sync_without_scope_has_none`): `scope` is optional, after `more`, `{"read": …, "write": …}` with each side `"all"`, `"none"` (`sync_scope_none*`: the owner shares nothing, or lets the agent write nothing) or a non-empty list of names matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,63}$`; parsers deduplicate and sort the lists, keep names they do not know and ignore unknown keys inside the object. `["none"]` is a list with one name, never "nothing". Any other shape (not an object, `null`, a side missing, another word, `"NONE"`, a non-string or badly spelled name, an empty list) drops only the field: `/scope` is listed in `dropped` after the element drops and the message stays `ok`. The phone sends it in every relay sync message; a native webhook body has none. A parser that predates `"none"` drops such a scope as malformed; the phone still enforces each side independently: `read: "none"` stops Health-data uploads, while `write: "none"` rejects writes with `type_not_in_scope`.
- **Own deletions**: the phone reports `deleted_by_user` for a command only when the user deleted the object of the command's current version after it was `applied`: a deleted object whose sync identifier is exactly `syncky:<hub_id>:<paired agent member_id>:<command_id>` and whose `sync_version` equals the ledger's `last_version`. The phone reports it whatever the agent's read scope: a type the agent may write but not read is checked for such deletions too, and the own deletion is never uploaded as a `deleted` item. The deletions HealthKit makes for an update or a delete carry an older version and are never reported; every other `syncky:` object stays echo. Consumers may project `deleted_by_user` as terminal for that version; the thin agent retains every raw reply without a command ledger. The phone answers a resend of that version with `deleted_by_user` again.
- **`sync_version` is boundary-only**: the `collectedJson` deletions carry it from iOS to the core (`bridge-json.json` `collected_with_sync_version`), the inner parser ignores it as an unknown field, and it never reaches a relay message or a webhook body. The same holds for `user_entered` on samples (`collected_every_object_kind`), which only the Health Auto Export `symptoms` array uses.
- **Object kinds** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_state_of_mind`, `sync_scored_assessments`, `sync_audiogram`, `sync_activity_summary`, `sync_workout_*`, `sync_*_part` and their `sync_drop_*` cases): enumerated fields carry the names of the type's `enums` table in `types.json`, never raw values; an unknown name drops the sample. The workout's `location`, `metadata` and array fields are optional for parsers (defaults `location: "unknown"`, `metadata: {}`, empty arrays) and always written by emitters; a `statistics` entry whose `type` is not a catalog quantity is skipped, not dropped. An activity summary's uuid must be `activity_summary:<date>` and has no `start`, `end` or `source`; receivers replace a stored day when the envelope `seq` is higher (the characteristic rule) and never count it as a duplicate.
- **Series parts** (`series-parts.json`): a wire `workout_route` or `heartbeat_series` needs integer `part` and `parts` with `0 ≤ part < parts ≤ 100000` and `0 ≤ count ≤ 10^7`; anything else, including a missing `part`, drops with the single code `bad_part`. A bad tuple drops the whole part. Parts are keyed `(device, uuid, part)`: an identical repeat is ignored, a differing repeat or header makes the set inconsistent (discarded, later parts ignored for 7 days), a set completes when every index is present and the joined array length equals `count`, and an incomplete set expires after 7 days. The reassembled sample has no `part`/`parts` and equals `reassembled` exactly. Splitters cut by the emitted byte size, not by a point count, so `parts` only matches when an implementation emits the same bytes.
- **Webhook signatures**: the verifier compares the whole `v1=<lowercase hex>` header value in constant time, so uppercase hex is `bad_signature`.
- **CSV and line protocol bodies** (`webhook-requests.json` `csv_*`, `influx_*`): CSV uses CRLF, quotes a field only when it holds `,`, `"`, CR or LF, writes times in the sample's `local_offset_s` (`±HH:MM`) or `Z`, `user_entered` as `true`/`false` on sample rows and empty on characteristic and deletion rows, and a deletion as `type,uuid,,,,,deleted,,,`. Line protocol sorts tags by key, leaves out empty tags, escapes `\`, `,` and space (and `=` in tags), turns tabs and line breaks in tags and strings into spaces, and writes the start in nanoseconds. Numbers use the JSON number spelling of the core (`812`, not `812.0`).
- **Basic auth** (`native_basic_signed`, `csv_basic_signed_every_kind`): `Authorization: Basic base64(<auth.user>:<token secret>)` after the signature headers; the user is printable ASCII without `:`.
- **Server replies and results** (`test-vectors/webhook-exchanges.json`): a reply is signed `X-Syncky-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` over `<X-Syncky-Delivery of the request>.<t>.<raw reply body>`, unlike the request signature, which has its own timestamp header; the results request body is `{"v":1,"type":"results","results":[…]}` whose entries have the ack shape of `inner-sync.schema.json` (`command_id`, `version`, `status`, `reason`), sent with `X-Syncky-Kind: results` instead of `X-Syncky-Format`. The file's cases carry a `kind`. A `reply` case is one server reply as the phone checks it: `url` (http or https), `signing`, `secret`, the request's `delivery`, `t`, the phone's clock `now`, `content_type`, `body`, `signature` (or null), `signature_valid` (the signature is the exact one for `delivery`, `t` and `body`, whatever the time window) and `expect`, which is `{"verdict":"commands","count":n}`, `{"verdict":"empty"}` or `{"verdict":"ignored","reason":…}` with the reasons `too_large`, `not_json`, `not_commands`, `unsigned` and `bad_signature`. The http replies answer request 0 of `webhook-requests.json` `native_bearer_signed_every_kind` (its `X-Syncky-Delivery`, its HMAC secret and its timestamp as `t`), so a receiver replaying that request signs `signed_http` byte for byte; `signed_http` is two writes, `c_1` `dietary_water` and `c_2` `apple_exercise_time`, and `signed_http_delete` deletes `c_1` (version 2) in a later exchange. The `results_request` case is what the phone sends after `signed_http` (`c_1` applied, `c_2` rejected `type_not_allowed`), and one `test_request` per format is the Check-connection request (the format's body for no changes, `delivery.test: true` in native, an empty influx body); both carry the `destination`, its `secrets`, and the byte-exact `headers` and `body`. Phone/schema tests cover these reply and request bytes; the agent's `selftest` checks `webhook-signatures.json`. `examples/minimal-server` signs `signed_http` byte for byte.
- **Sync identifiers per source**: agent `syncky:<hub_id>:<member_id>:<command_id>`, server `syncky:wh_<id>:<command_id>`, file import `syncky:import:<16 hex>:<row>`; the source is always local (the pairing, the destination, the file's hash), never taken from a reply or a file.
- **Numbers**: integers in JSON bodies are value-based (`1`, `1.0`, `1e0` are 1; fractional, string, boolean, null, negative and ≥ 2^53 values are not integers). Emitters write an integral finite value as a JSON integer (`812`, not `812.0`). Fractional formatting is not pinned; compare by value.
- **Timestamps**: emit UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` when the milliseconds are 0, otherwise exactly 3 fraction digits (sub-millisecond truncated). Accept `Z`/`z` or `±HH:MM`, uppercase or lowercase `t`, and 0–9 fraction digits; reject everything else, including calendar-invalid dates, hour 24 and `:60`.

## Schema rules

- JSON Schema 2020-12. Each file has an `$id` (`https://syncky.app/protocol/schemas/<file>`) and a `$defs` map; validate a document against `<$id>#/$defs/<name>`.
- Only local `#/$defs/…` refs, no cross-file refs (the vector schema carries its own copy of the submitted envelope).
- `pattern`, never the `format` keyword, so Ajv `strict: true` and networknt need no format plugins. Calendar validity of timestamps (Feb 30) and base64url canonical tails are checked by the implementations, not by the schemas.
- The schemas stay Ajv-strict clean: an explicit `type` next to every type-specific keyword, `anyOf` instead of type arrays, and every `required` name declared in the same schema's `properties`. The core checks these rules together with the meta-schema.
- Envelopes reject unknown top-level keys; inner messages, system events and samples allow them. Inner-message timestamps use the emit form (see Timestamps above); envelope and system-event timestamps use the accept form.
- In `inner-messages.json` and `bridge-json.json`, the `json` field of a case is the exact JSON text as a string, so unparsable and non-object inputs are representable and the bytes are preserved.

## Diagnostics data and consent controls

New senders add optional visible envelope metadata `diagnostics=request|reply|archive`: request/reply require `kind=control`, archive requires `kind=data`; ordinary traffic omits it and system events cannot carry it. This reveals the claimed diagnostics purpose to Relay, which checks shape and routes traffic but cannot decrypt or verify the inner contents. Both HPKE Auth and payload AEAD bind the marker after any `|control` suffix as `|diagnostics=<value>`; updated receivers reject marker/inner mismatch before dispatch and never fall back to legacy AAD. Unmarked older diagnostics and already-sealed legacy retries remain accepted unchanged. Old Dev/pre-marker receivers cannot open honestly marked traffic and must update; deploy relay support before using new senders and update both endpoints together, without stripping markers on errors.

A newly queued marked request triggers a best-effort generic visible `diagnostics_request` push on every plan, outside ordinary push scheduling. It carries the already-visible envelope `msg_id`, no request reference or report contents. Remote taps match that id to the authenticated pending request; local `diagnostics-request-<ref>` taps match the exact reference. A notification tap opens Review for its matching pending request once available; expired, answered, replaced, unmatched or re-paired notices only open Diagnostics without selecting another request. Receipt alone prepares nothing, and only Confirm sends the approved preview.

Envelope `v=1` and kinds remain `data`, `control` and relay-generated `system`; the optional `diagnostics` field adds visible purpose metadata without a new kind or version. `type=diagnostics` is a phone-to-agent data inner, never a Health sample or command. The complete canonical UTF-8 JSON is at most 180000 bytes, sent to one confirmed agent within the 262144-byte serialized envelope cap. Its `archive_ref`, optional `request_ref` and peer references are 32 lowercase hex characters, derived with domain-separated SHA-256; the diagnostics report contains closed findings, aggregate counts, times, build metadata and safe history, never raw hub/member ids, names, credentials, URLs, Health values/type names or command payloads. Unknown fields are rejected. `inner-messages.json` pins normalization, invalid fields, bounds and cross-kind rejection; `envelopes.json` pins encrypted diagnostics and request/reply round trips. Vector bytes win over prose.

Canonical submitted JSON orders the existing required fields `v, msg_id, kind, from, created_at, recipients, nonce, ciphertext`, inserting `access` or `diagnostics` immediately after `kind` when present. Null, empty, unknown and incompatible marker values are invalid. Missing marker preserves the prior canonical bytes. Exact AAD in both crypto layers is UTF-8 of `syncky-v1|<hub_id>|<msg_id>|<from>` + (`|control` for control) + (`|diagnostics=<value>` when present), in that fixed order; HPKE info stays `syncky-cek-v1`. Request/control must decrypt to `diagnostics_request`, reply/control to `diagnostics_reply`, archive/data to `diagnostics`. A mismatch is `inner_invalid`; stripped, added or changed markers fail authentication, with no legacy-AAD fallback. The generated positive, shape and negative vectors cover these rules while retaining unmarked cases. A paired sender can claim a lane with legacy-AAD ciphertext that an old receiver may still act on; the small relay lane bounds this residual abuse. Marker authentication protects updated recipients and does not let Relay verify contents.

`diagnostics_request` is an agent-to-phone encrypted control inner with `request_ref`, `created_at` and `expires_at` exactly 24 hours later. `diagnostics_reply` goes back with that reference and `outcome=declined|expired`; reasons are `user`, `pending_limit`, `rate_limited` for declined or `deadline` for expired. Controls retain the 4096-byte envelope cap. A confirmed diagnostics report carries the request reference. Consumers correlate it through the durable raw inbox; there is no agent-local request state or diagnostics validator. Relay acceptance and transport ACK alone do not prove diagnostics report receipt. Old clients may skip unknown controls and the request expires; the minimal agent authenticates/decrypts data, generically skips non-sync contents and persists/ACKs without diagnostics report storage.

Request arrival only records pending state. A matching notification tap opens Review; Home opens Diagnostics. Review prepares and freezes the preview, View/Download expose those bytes, Confirm authorizes those same bytes to that agent, and Decline queues only a reply. Rebuilding invalidates consent. The phone keeps one pending request per agent and a 24-hour expiry; phone retries do not reset deadlines. The phone permits at most one diagnostics report per rolling 24 hours per agent pairing, counting both manual Send and a confirmed request on its own clock; Send and Confirm show when they become available again. View and Download are unlimited. The thin agent sends explicitly requested JSON through generic CLI/MCP send and reads diagnostics or diagnostics_reply through inbox. It imposes no local cooldown or request admission policy; the phone owns those decisions. Sealed outbox retries and raw inbox persistence use protected files, without SQLite. Marked traffic uses an independent relay lane on every plan: 30 new envelopes per hub per UTC day and at most 2 MiB/100 outstanding rows per hub by default, outside ordinary control quotas, agent data-send budgets and general queue capacity. Its token RPM allowance is separate from ordinary calls, including ACKs. HTTP `429 rate_limited` distinguishes `details.reason=diagnostics_quota` (Retry-After to UTC midnight), `diagnostics_queue_full` (300 seconds) and ordinary `queue_full`; RPM refusals have no lane-specific reason. Identical accepted retries spend no new daily/queue quota. Legacy unmarked traffic retains ordinary relay accounting. The diagnostics outbox lane retries independently of ordinary sends.

Local Check sends nothing. Separate explicit evidence refresh and diagnostics report preparation may read device-member-authenticated `GET /v1/hub/diagnostics` without diagnostics upload or sync. It returns caller-only push attempts beside last phone contact, existing agent poll/ACK evidence and scoped queue counts. APNs 200 means accepted, not delivered or proof of why iOS did not run. History is bounded to the hub's newest 50 sends within 48 hours; missing/stale evidence remains unknown. A missing route is explicit `unsupported_route`, while local Check/View/Download remain usable. Marked diagnostics reports retain `402 hub_unpaid|hub_suspended`; marked requests/replies remain admissible in active, unpaid and suspended hubs under diagnostics limits.

Phone history and manual pending diagnostics report retries expire after 48 hours; request-bound diagnostics reports stop sending at the original 24-hour request deadline. Matching pre-expiry diagnostics report/decline sends can resolve a local deadline expiry when processed within 48 hours of sending; pairing changes and post-expiry sends remain rejected. Terminal reply retries last 48 hours from the decision, independently of that request deadline. The thin agent retains every authentic diagnostics record in its raw inbox for 30 days from receipt, including repeated archive references under new envelopes. Read operations do not prune; receive startup/daily pruning and explicit owner-approved forget after revocation follow the ordinary inbox rules. Phone pruning runs when the app next executes. User-controlled downloaded copies and support attachments follow their destination's retention. Diagnostics are neither identity proof nor a complete access export; use the app's Privacy requests flow for verified Relay requests.

## Health access controls

`access: "request" | "reply"` is optional visible metadata on `kind=control` only, mapping to authenticated `access_request` (agent → confirmed phone) or `access_reply` (phone → requesting agent). `access` and `diagnostics` are mutually exclusive; neither appears on relay `system` events. Reject null, unknown, malformed, dual or wrong-kind markers. New access inners require the marker; the decrypted type must match it before dispatch, pairing exceptions or state mutation. The relay validates shape and retains the marker, but cannot verify encrypted semantics.

Canonical envelope order is `v, msg_id, kind, access?, diagnostics?, from, created_at, recipients, nonce, ciphertext`. Both HPKE Auth and payload AEAD use UTF-8 `syncky-v1|<hub_id>|<msg_id>|<from>` followed by optional `|control`, optional `|diagnostics=<value>`, optional `|access=<value>` in that order. Mutual exclusion permits at most one marker suffix. Unmarked/diagnostics bytes are unchanged. Added, stripped or changed markers and legacy-AAD ciphertext with an attached marker fail authentication; never fall back, strip a marker or reseal a persisted retry. Submission keys are strict; delivery still tolerates unrelated extra keys, but a malformed present marker is never absent.

Both inners are v1. `access_request` fields are `v, type, request_ref, created_at, expires_at, read, write` and optional `reason`. The reference is 32 lowercase hex characters; expiry is exactly creation plus 24 hours. Required read/write arrays are individually sorted/unique and jointly nonempty; the same name may occur on both sides. Validate read catalog/scope names (including `workout` and characteristics) and writability for writes independently of current scope. Reason is literal plain text, at most 200 Unicode code points, with invalid Unicode rejected; never interpret it as instructions or markup.

`access_reply` fields are `v, type, request_ref, decided_at, outcome, read, write`, with `next_available_at` only for limit outcomes. A `resolved` reply contains exactly the request's names/sides, one `{type, outcome}` per item; outcomes are `allowed`, `declined`, `needs_health_settings`. Request-level `expired`, `pending_limit`, `rate_limited` have empty read/write arrays; limits require availability time and never invent user declines. The stored request defines correlation and expected items. Strict field/direction/timestamp/cardinality rules live in [inner-system.schema.json](schemas/inner-system.schema.json), with marker shape in [envelope.schema.json](schemas/envelope.schema.json).

There is no item-count cap: before admission, both the serialized UTF-8 request envelope and the largest legal corresponding reply must fit 4096 bytes, including all fields, marker, timestamps, AEAD tag, base64url expansion and HPKE recipient overhead. Sealing and incoming validation enforce the same limit; never split an oversized request automatically.

The phone enforces one pending request per agent, a separate access admission of one per rolling 24 hours, exact 24-hour expiry and phone retries stopping at the original deadline. Five-minute future skew and an admission-plus-24-hour clamp follow diagnostics. Decline starts a seven-day type-wide read/write cooldown from the phone's decision time. One cooling type refuses the whole request. Limits/expiry/Health settings outcomes create no user-decline cooldown. The phone persists correlation, decisions, cooldowns and byte-identical retries under the pairing identity; revoke/unpair/re-pair clears its stale work. Late or conflicting replies never replace a committed phone decision. The thin agent keeps every raw reply and imposes no local admission or cooldown policy; callers correlate request references and inspect phone outcomes through inbox.

Queued and transport ACK mean persistence, not user consent. Only explicit phone confirmation changes selection and stored scope; a reply alone never changes cached effective scope, which arrives on the next ordinary sync. Allow adds only approved types to Health selection, without selecting their categories. Existing selected categories and individually allowed types are preserved. Allowed writes turn on the global **Allow writing to Health** toggle for all selected writable types; agent scope and iOS write permission still apply. Existing read `all` stays `all` and follows later Health selection changes. Approved reads turn `none` into a chosen list and are unioned and sorted into existing read lists. If writing was off or the agent's effective write allowance was empty, its write scope becomes only the approved write types, even from `all` or an absent scope; otherwise existing write scope is unioned as before. Decline revokes nothing. Both `allowed` and `needs_health_settings` mean Allow in Syncky. Health read authorization is unobservable; successful sheet completion and empty data prove neither a grant nor denial. Previously answered reads and denied/undetermined writes need conditional Health settings guidance. Asking never authorizes writing a Health value.

Access is ordinary relay control traffic: shared token RPM, non-active control quota and ordinary queue caps/429 Retry-After apply. It has no diagnostics exemption or relay lifecycle state. Endpoint scheduling stays independent of diagnostics and ordinary sends. A newly accepted request queues a generic visible `access_request` alert on every plan, with category `access_request`, `msg_id` and collapse id `access_request:<msg_id>`; no type names, reason or request reference reach APNs. No extra silent wake is scheduled for the same request. Receipt/tap never grants access or presents Health authorization. Exact remote msg-id/local reference routing selects only a live matching request under the current pairing; stale notices never select another request.

Deploy relay support before updated senders, and update both endpoints. Old clients may fail to open or skip access controls; safely ACK poison messages, allow expiry and update, never downgrade AAD. Minimal/browser examples authenticate the marker/inner match and skip unsupported access controls without exposing their contents; their cursor/ACK and later sync processing continue. Request/decision storage and consent UI belong to the phone; the thin agent offers generic send/inbox and retains raw messages.

The thin agent reads the generated messages.json table and bundled/verified inner schemas for optional send validation. It retains authenticated raw JSON for 30 days without a Health parser, ledger or SQLite; phone/schema tests own feature-policy and reassembly conformance.
